summary:
"Abandoned but Not Forgotten" is an interactive, educational web platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project aims to recover and share the stories of the machines, vehicles, and space probes that NASA left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space, transforming scientific information into accessible and engaging experiences.

We have developed an interactive digital library where users can explore space missions through virtual books, historical data, and 3D visualizations. We have also included an educational game zone featuring word searches, quizzes, and a three-dimensional lunar expedition, in which players operate a rover, discover historical artifacts, and manage their energy levels to complete the mission.

Our proposal addresses the challenge of bringing space-related knowledge to the general public, especially children and students, through interactive learning. We seek to preserve the legacy of space exploration, spark scientific curiosity, and inspire new generations to discover the universe.
details:
Project Details: Abandoned but Not Forgotten

Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive educational website developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project focuses on telling the stories of spacecraft, rovers, satellites, and scientific equipment that NASA left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space.

How does our project work?

Our website features a virtual library where users can explore NASA missions through interactive digital books. Visitors can search for specific objects, filter missions by location, and discover historical information through visual content and animated 3D models.

The platform also includes three educational games:

  • Space Word Search: Players find the names of spacecraft and discover interesting facts.
  • Space Quiz: Users answer questions about NASA missions and receive explanations.
  • 3D Lunar Expedition: Players drive a rover across the Moon, explore historical objects, and manage their battery power to complete the mission.

Users can also suggest new NASA objects or missions to expand the virtual library.

What are the benefits and expected impact?

Our project makes space exploration easier to understand, especially for children and students. Instead of only reading scientific information, users can interact with historical missions, explore 3D environments, and learn through educational games.

We expect our platform to encourage curiosity, improve interest in science and technology, and inspire future generations of scientists, engineers, and explorers.

What technologies did we use?

Our project is a web-based application that combines interactive interfaces, educational content, and 3D experiences.

The platform uses web technologies such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for its interface and interactive functionality. It is deployed online using Render, allowing users to access the website through a browser without installing additional software.

The project also uses publicly available NASA information as a reference for its educational content.

What makes our project creative?

Our creativity comes from transforming abandoned space technology into an interactive learning experience.

Instead of focusing only on famous NASA discoveries, we tell the stories of machines that completed their missions but remain part of space exploration history.

We combine a virtual library, animated 3D scenes, and educational games to make scientific learning more engaging.

What factors did our team consider?

Our team focused on accessibility, educational value, usability, and creativity.

We wanted to create a platform that children and students could use without advanced scientific knowledge. We also considered the importance of presenting understandable information based on NASA's public resources.

By combining storytelling, technology, and interactive activities, our project aims to show that even machines left behind in space still have valuable stories to tell.
